questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.sub_topic: How the sepoys began their rising
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II, according to how risings often began in 1857.

List-I (Object or place)
(A) Evening gun or bugle
(B) Bell of arms
(C) Treasury
(D) Jail and telegraph office

List-II (What the sepoys did)
(I) Attacked them as symbols of British authority
(II) Seized it for its weapons
(III) Treated it as the signal to rise
(IV) Plundered it for its money
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: The evening gun or bugle was the signal (III), and the bell of arms was seized for weapons (II). The treasury was plundered (IV), and the jail and telegraph office were attacked as symbols of authority (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the signal and the bell of arms. (B) swaps the bell of arms and the treasury. (C) swaps the treasury and the jail.
Key point: The similar pattern in many places suggests planning and coordination.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about crops in the Mughal period:
(A) In most places there were at least two crops a year, in the kharif and rabi seasons.
(B) Bengal is said to have grown about fifty varieties of rice.
(C) New crops from the Americas, such as tomatoes, potatoes and chillies, were introduced.
(D) Peasants grew only food grains and no cash crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT. There were usually two harvests, Bengal had many rice varieties, and New World crops arrived.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Peasants also grew cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane. Options (A), (C) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Agriculture was organised to meet both subsistence and trade.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: Besides British targets, rebels in many places also attacked:
options: A) Peasants of their own villages
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Moneylenders and the rich
Why: In many places rebels attacked moneylenders and the rich, whom they saw as allies of the British and as oppressors.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) were not usual targets.
Key point: The revolt also expressed social grievances within Indian society.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Control at the centre shifts to the Aravidu lineage
(B) Abdur Razzaq visits Vijayanagara
(C) Krishnadeva Raya dies
(D) Domingo Paes visits the city
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: Abdur Razzaq came in the 1440s, and Paes in the early 1520s. Krishnadeva Raya died in 1529, and by 1542 control had shifted to the Aravidu lineage.
Why not the others: (A) puts Paes before Abdur Razzaq. (C) puts Krishnadeva Raya's death before Paes's visit. (D) puts the Aravidu shift before his death.
Key point: Foreign visitors left valuable accounts of the city at its height.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.sub_topic: Portuguese aims on the west coast
questions.question: In the early sixteenth century, the Portuguese on the west coast of India tried to:
options: A) Buy the city of Vijayanagara
C) Convert the rulers to Christianity
D) Set up trading and military stations
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Set up trading and military stations
Why: The Portuguese tried to set up trading and military stations on the west coast.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not what NCERT describes.
Key point: Their superior military technology made them important players in the region.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Khalifa
(B) Dargah
(C) Urs
(D) Barakat

List-II (Meaning)
(I) The tomb-shrine of a Sufi saint
(II) The anniversary of a saint's death
(III) Spiritual grace
(IV) A successor named by the shaikh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: A khalifa was a successor (IV), and a dargah the tomb-shrine of a saint (I). Urs marks the anniversary of the saint's death (II), and barakat is spiritual grace (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps khalifa and dargah. (B) swaps dargah and urs. (C) swaps urs and barakat.
Key point: Pilgrims visited dargahs to seek the saint's barakat.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The *Nalayira Divyaprabandham*, the anthology of the Alvars' compositions, was frequently described as the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Tamil Veda
Why: The anthology was described as the Tamil Veda, claiming it was as important as the four Sanskrit Vedas.
Why not the others: (A) is a title claimed by the Mahabharata. (C) and (D) are not its titles.
Key point: Tamil devotional poetry gained great prestige in the region.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Lathyal
(B) Benami
(C) Kist
(D) Mahal

List-II (Meaning)
(I) A purchase made in a fictitious name
(II) A strongman kept by a zamindar
(III) A revenue estate
(IV) An instalment of revenue
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: A lathyal was a zamindar's strongman (II), and a benami purchase was made in a fictitious name (I). A kist was an instalment (IV), and a mahal a revenue estate (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps lathyal and benami. (C) swaps benami and kist. (D) swaps kist and mahal.
Key point: Zamindars used such methods to hold on to their estates.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: The only means of grinding cereals in Harappan settlements appear to have been:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Saddle querns
Why: Saddle querns, made of hard stone, appear to have been the only means of grinding cereals.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) were not used by the Harappans.
Key point: Querns are an example of artefacts classified by their function.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: "Lal, Bal and Pal" refers to the Radical leaders Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Bipin Chandra Pal
Why: Pal was Bipin Chandra Pal, from Bengal.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) were Moderates.
Key point: The Radicals called for more militant opposition to British rule.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Agriculture could expand in the Mughal period partly because of:
options: A) Abundant land and mobile peasants
C) Canals built by the Portuguese
D) A ban on cash crops
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Abundant land and mobile peasants
Why: Abundant land, available labour and the mobility of peasants allowed cultivation to expand.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not true of the period.
Key point: Peasants could move to new land when conditions became hard.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Salt March:
(A) It was the first nationalist activity in which women took part in large numbers.
(B) It made the British realise that they would have to devolve some power to Indians.
(C) It was widely reported in the European and American press.
(D) Gandhi called it off after the violence at Chauri Chaura.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. Chauri Chaura led Gandhi to call off Non-Cooperation in 1922, not the Salt March.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (B), (C) and (D) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: The British responded by holding a series of Round Table Conferences.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question:
Arrange the following events of the Buddha's life in the order in which they took place:
(A) He gives his first sermon at Sarnath
(B) He is born at Lumbini
(C) He passes away at Kusinagara
(D) He attains enlightenment at Bodh Gaya
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: The Buddha was born at Lumbini and attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. He gave his first sermon at Sarnath and passed away at Kusinagara.
Why not the others: (A) puts enlightenment before birth. (C) puts the sermon before enlightenment. (D) puts his death before the sermon.
Key point: All four places became important centres of Buddhist pilgrimage.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Since the Company had decreed that the property of women would not be taken over, the Raja of Burdwan transferred part of his zamindari to his ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Mother
Why: The Raja transferred part of his zamindari to his mother.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) were not who received the transfer.
Key point: Zamindars found many ways to get round the auction of their estates.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.sub_topic: The body that framed the Constitution
questions.question: The Constitution of India was framed by the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Constituent Assembly
Why: The Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly between December 1946 and November 1949.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) did not frame it.
Key point: The Assembly debated every provision before it was adopted.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.sub_topic: Who besides the provinces sat in the Assembly
questions.question: Apart from members elected by the provincial legislatures, the Constituent Assembly also included representatives of the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Princely states
Why: The princely states were also represented in the Constituent Assembly.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) were not represented.
Key point: Bringing the princely states into the Union was a major task of these years.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.sub_topic: Order of early states and sources
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Sixteen mahajanapadas emerge
(B) Banabhatta writes the *Harshacharita*
(C) Colossal Kushana statues are set up at Mat, near Mathura
(D) Megasthenes visits the court of Chandragupta Maurya
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (D), (C), (B)
Why: The mahajanapadas emerged in the sixth century BCE, and Megasthenes came c. 300 BCE. The Kushana statues date to the first centuries CE, and the *Harshacharita* to the seventh century CE.
Why not the others: (A) puts Megasthenes before the mahajanapadas. (B) puts the Kushanas before Megasthenes. (C) puts the *Harshacharita* before the Kushana statues.
Key point: Texts, statues and inscriptions all help date early states.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Leader)
(A) Rajendra Prasad
(B) C. Rajagopalachari
(C) Govind Ballabh Pant
(D) Vallabh Bhai Patel

List-II (Region)
(I) United Provinces
(II) Gujarat
(III) Madras
(IV) Bihar
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Rajendra Prasad came from Bihar (IV), and C. Rajagopalachari from Madras (III). Govind Ballabh Pant came from the United Provinces (I), and Patel from Gujarat (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Prasad and Rajagopalachari. (B) swaps Rajagopalachari and Pant. (D) swaps Pant and Patel.
Key point: Gandhi drew new leaders from many regions into the Congress.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Megasthenes' *Indica* has not survived as a complete book. It is known today through:
options: A) A copper-plate copy kept at Pataliputra
B) Fragments quoted by later writers
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Fragments quoted by later writers
Why: The *Indica* survives only in fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not how the text has come down to us.
Key point: Historians must read such fragments carefully, since later writers chose what to quote.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about early cities:
(A) Many cities grew along routes of communication, by rivers or on land routes.
(B) Short votive inscriptions in cities record gifts by washermen, weavers, scribes, carpenters and merchants.
(C) A fine glossy pottery called Northern Black Polished Ware has been found at urban sites.
(D) Cities had no links with the surrounding countryside.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT. Cities grew along routes, votive inscriptions record many kinds of donors, and NBPW is found at urban sites.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Cities depended on the countryside for food and raw materials. Options (B), (C) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Votive inscriptions give rare glimpses of ordinary town dwellers.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The stupa at Sanchi is located in present-day:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Madhya Pradesh
Why: Sanchi is in Madhya Pradesh, near Bhopal.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) have other Buddhist sites. (D) has Amaravati.
Key point: Sanchi is one of the best-preserved early Buddhist sites.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: Under the compromise on language, English was to continue to be used for official purposes for:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Fifteen years
Why: The Language Committee proposed that English should continue for official purposes for the first fifteen years.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the period proposed.
Key point: The change to Hindi was meant to be gradual.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: To protect themselves from raids, zamindars on the plains near the Rajmahal hills often:
options: A) Moved their estates to Calcutta
B) Paid tribute to the hill chiefs
C) Joined the Paharias in raids
D) Asked the Mughal emperor for troops
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Paid tribute to the hill chiefs
Why: Zamindars often bought peace by paying a regular tribute to the Paharia chiefs.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not what NCERT describes.
Key point: The Paharias also controlled routes through the hills.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: Inscriptions are writings:
options: A) Copied by hand on palm leaves
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Engraved on hard surfaces
Why: Inscriptions are engraved on hard surfaces such as stone, metal or pottery.
Why not the others: (A) describes manuscripts. (B) and (D) are not inscriptions.
Key point: Inscriptions often record the achievements of the people who had them made.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: Guru Nanak expressed his ideas through hymns in Punjabi called ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Shabad
Why: Guru Nanak's hymns are called shabad. They were sung in various ragas.
Why not the others: (B) were Virashaiva sayings. (C) were Kabir's upside-down sayings. (D) is a hymn sung in qawwali.
Key point: His hymns were later included in the *Adi Granth*.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.sub_topic: Why the sultan welcomed Ibn Battuta
questions.question: Ibn Battuta was welcomed in Delhi because Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq was known as a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Patron of learning
Why: Ibn Battuta was attracted by the sultan's reputation as a generous patron of arts and letters.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) do not describe the sultan.
Key point: The sultan made him the qazi, or judge, of Delhi.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: In Harappan archaeology, a "sealing" is:
options: A) A stone used for weighing
B) A drain that is covered with bricks
C) The wall round the Citadel
D) The impression of a seal on clay
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The impression of a seal on clay
Why: A sealing is the impression left when a seal is pressed on wet clay, for instance on a bag of goods.
Why not the others: (A) describes a weight. (B) describes a covered drain. (C) describes a city wall.
Key point: Sealings helped identify the sender of goods.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Each chapter of al-Biruni's *Kitab-ul-Hind* usually:
options: B) Retold a story from the epics
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Opened with a question
Why: Each chapter began with a question, gave a description based on Sanskrit traditions, and ended with a comparison with other cultures.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) do not describe his method.
Key point: Some scholars think the clear structure came from his training in mathematics.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: The capital of Awadh at the time of its annexation was:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Lucknow
Why: Lucknow was the capital of Awadh.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were other towns of north India.
Key point: The siege of the Lucknow Residency was one of the major events of 1857.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about how archaeologists study Harappan artefacts:
(A) They classify finds by material, such as stone, clay, metal, bone and ivory.
(B) They also classify finds by function, for example as tools, ornaments or objects for ritual.
(C) Where objects have not survived, they sometimes rely on indirect evidence, such as depictions in sculpture.
(D) The function of every artefact can always be identified with certainty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT. Archaeologists sort finds by material and by function, and use indirect evidence where needed.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Deciding what an object was used for is often difficult. Options (A), (B) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Archaeologists also look at where an object was found, inside a house, in a drain or in a grave.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law, is on the coast of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Gujarat
Why: Dandi is on the coast of Gujarat.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are other coastal regions.
Key point: The march from Sabarmati to Dandi took about three weeks.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.sub_topic: From Hodges to the end of the cotton boom
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) The Santhal Pargana is created
(B) The cotton boom in the Deccan ends as American cotton revives
(C) William Hodges paints the Rajmahal hills
(D) Francis Buchanan travels through the Rajmahal hills
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: Hodges painted the hills in the 1780s, and Buchanan travelled there in 1810–11. The Santhal Pargana was created after the revolt of 1855–56, and the cotton boom ended after the American Civil War in 1865.
Why not the others: (A) puts Buchanan before Hodges. (B) puts the Santhal Pargana before Buchanan. (D) puts the end of the boom before the Santhal Pargana.
Key point: Images and travel journals are sources for colonial rural history.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: The provincial elections of 1946, whose legislatures chose the Constituent Assembly, were held on the basis of:
options: D) Votes of the princes alone
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A limited franchise
Why: The elections were held on a limited franchise, not on universal adult franchise.
Why not the others: (B) came only with the Constitution. (C) and (D) are not how the elections were held.
Key point: Members were nonetheless drawn from many regions and backgrounds.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II, according to Ibn Battuta's account.

List-I (Subject)
(A) Indian soil
(B) Bazaars
(C) Daulatabad
(D) The postal system

List-II (Observation)
(I) Rivalled Delhi in size
(II) Let merchants send information and remit credit
(III) So fertile that two crops a year were grown
(IV) Had a mosque and a temple, and places for performances
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: The soil was fertile enough for two crops (III), and bazaars had a mosque, a temple and places for performances (IV). Daulatabad rivalled Delhi (I), and the postal system helped merchants (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the soil and the bazaars. (C) swaps the bazaars and Daulatabad. (D) swaps Daulatabad and the postal system.
Key point: Ibn Battuta found Indian cities full of opportunity.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: At Meerut, shortly before the outbreak, sepoys who had refused to use the new cartridges were:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Dismissed and jailed
Why: Eighty-five sepoys were dismissed from service and sentenced to ten years in jail.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not what happened.
Key point: The punishment angered other sepoys, who broke out the next day.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: The *Ain-i Akbari* was written in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Persian
Why: The *Ain-i Akbari* was written in Persian, the language of the Mughal court.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) were not its language.
Key point: Persian was the language of administration under the Mughals.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about early Sufis:
(A) They criticised the dogmatic definitions and scholastic methods of the theologians.
(B) They sought salvation through intense devotion to and love for God.
(C) By the eleventh century Sufism had grown into a well-developed movement.
(D) They rejected the Qur'an altogether.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. Sufis sought an interpretation of the Qur'an based on their personal experience.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (D) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: Sufis organised communities around the hospice, or khanqah.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.sub_topic: The Muslim quarter of the city
questions.question: In the north-eastern part of Vijayanagara's urban core was a Muslim residential quarter. Its tombs and mosques are notable because their architecture:
options: A) Resembles the mandapas of Hampi's temples
B) Copies the pyramids of ancient Egypt
C) Follows a purely Portuguese style of building
D) Uses no stone or brick at all
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Resembles the mandapas of Hampi's temples
Why: The tombs and mosques resemble the mandapas found in the temples of Hampi.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) do not describe these buildings.
Key point: Building traditions were shared across communities in the city.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Name)
(A) Magan
(B) Dilmun
(C) Shortughai
(D) Mohenjodaro

List-II (Present-day location)
(I) Sindh, in Pakistan
(II) Probably Oman
(III) Probably Bahrain
(IV) Afghanistan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: Magan was probably Oman (II), and Dilmun probably Bahrain (III). Shortughai is in Afghanistan (IV), and Mohenjodaro is in Sindh (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Magan and Dilmun. (C) swaps Dilmun and Shortughai. (D) swaps Shortughai and Mohenjodaro.
Key point: Magan and Dilmun are named in Mesopotamian texts about long-distance trade.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.question: At the Second Round Table Conference, Gandhi claimed that the Congress represented all of India. This claim was challenged by:
options: A) The members of the Viceroy's council
B) The League, the princes and Ambedkar
D) The British Labour Party in London
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The League, the princes and Ambedkar
Why: The Muslim League, the princes and B.R. Ambedkar challenged the claim.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not the challengers NCERT names.
Key point: The conference ended without agreement.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: For his Brahmana friends, al-Biruni translated the works of the Greek mathematician ____ into Sanskrit.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Euclid
Why: Al-Biruni translated Euclid's works into Sanskrit.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) were other Greek thinkers.
Key point: Al-Biruni also translated Sanskrit works, such as Patanjali's work on grammar, into Arabic.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, roughly what share of India's population lived in villages?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) About 85 per cent
Why: About 85 per cent of the population lived in villages.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are far too low.
Key point: This is why agrarian society is central to the history of the Mughal empire.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Buddhist texts:
(A) All Buddhist texts were written down during the Buddha's lifetime.
(B) As Buddhism spread to Sri Lanka, texts such as the *Dipavamsa* and the *Mahavamsa* were written.
(C) Some of the oldest texts are in Pali, while later compositions are in Sanskrit.
(D) Pilgrims from China took texts back to their homeland, where they were translated.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) only
Why: Only (A) is false. The Buddha taught orally, and his teachings were compiled by his followers after his death.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: Fa Xian and Xuan Zang travelled from China in search of Buddhist texts.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: The Buddha taught a path between severe penance and self-indulgence. This is often called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Middle path
Why: The Buddha taught a middle path of moderation, avoiding both extremes.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not how his teaching is described.
Key point: He stressed right conduct and individual effort.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Structure)
(A) The "king's palace"
(B) The "audience hall"
(C) The Mahanavami dibba
(D) The Kamalapuram tank

List-II (Description)
(I) The largest of the enclosures
(II) Its water was carried by a channel to the royal centre
(III) A massive platform linked with a festival
(IV) A high platform with slots for wooden pillars
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: The "king's palace" is the largest enclosure (I), and the "audience hall" has slots for wooden pillars (IV). The Mahanavami dibba is a massive festival platform (III), and the Kamalapuram tank's water reached the royal centre (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the palace and the audience hall. (B) swaps the audience hall and the dibba. (D) swaps the dibba and the tank.
Key point: Names such as "audience hall" were given by later scholars, not the builders.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.sub_topic: Whom a gotra was named after
questions.question:
Read the following source passage and answer the question that follows.

From about 1000 BCE onwards, Brahmanas in particular classified people into gotras. Each gotra was named after a Vedic seer, and everyone who belonged to it was regarded as his descendant. Two rules about gotra were especially important. When a woman married, she was expected to give up her father's gotra and take her husband's. And members of the same gotra could not marry one another.

Inscriptions of the Satavahana rulers, who governed parts of western India and the Deccan, allow historians to test whether these rules were followed. Several Satavahana kings were identified through metronymics, names derived from their mothers. Gotami-puta Siri-Satakani, for instance, means Siri-Satakani, son of Gotami. Gotami is the feminine form of Gotama, the name of a Vedic seer and of a gotra.

The inscriptions suggest that a number of Satavahana queens kept the gotra names of their fathers instead of taking their husbands'. Some of them even belonged to the same gotra as their husbands, which went against the ideal of marrying outside the gotra. Marriages within the kin group were common among several communities in south India. Even so, succession to the Satavahana throne was generally patrilineal.

Question: According to the passage, each gotra was named after:
options: A) A river of the region
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A Vedic seer
Why: The passage says each gotra was named after a Vedic seer, and its members were regarded as his descendants.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not mentioned in the passage.
Key point: Gotra was an important part of Brahmanical ideas about descent and marriage.

Question: What does the Satavahana evidence suggest about the Brahmanical rules on gotra?
options: A) They were followed everywhere without exception
B) They were invented by the Satavahanas
C) They gave mothers control of the throne
D) They were not followed by everyone
questions.explanation:
